about.ADV1010:
The Advisor reads the register, the organisation, the plan, the qualifications, the accounts and the backups, and lists what looks wrong, from the most serious to simple tips. Each point says why it matters and what to do; open it to see the records concerned.

It shows only what you may already read, and it changes nothing: you decide and correct in the usual screens.
about.ATT2010: Upload the attendance workbook of the day. The calculation engine is locked: it gives exactly the numbers the previous application gave. A file already uploaded is refused, and a bad file never replaces the last good result.
about.DSC1010: Each line says which violation it covers, from how many minutes it counts, over how many days repeats are counted, and the penalty for the 1st, 2nd, 3rd... time (the last one repeats). The schedule is the company's own and must be approved as the labour law requires: confirm the figures with your legal adviser.
about.DSC2010:
Violations are proposed from the attendance (late arrival, leaving early, absence, no record) against the planned shift, with the penalty the schedule gives for the first, second, third time. A day on approved leave, a rest day or a holiday is never a violation.

The HR officer proposes; a person with the right to decide (the line manager) applies the penalty or waives it. A decision is final and kept in the signed history. Penalties are written in days, never in money: payroll turns days into an amount later.

The law's limits are enforced: at most 5 days' deduction for one violation and 5 days in one month, a decision within 30 days of finding the violation, and a written investigation for more than one day.
about.EMP1010:
The employee register is the one source of truth for people in the whole ecosystem: manufacturing and accounting read it, they never change it.

Filter any column from its header, group the rows by a column from the column menu, or pick a preset above the grid. Double-click a row to edit it. A deleted employee goes to the Recycle Bin and can be restored; the history of every change is kept.
about.EMP2010:
Everything the system knows about one person, from every module: joining and placement, the team they lead, their user account, shifts and day changes, qualifications and when they expire, every attended day, lateness, absences, leave, violations and decisions, and what is planned for the next two weeks.

Press Play to watch the weeks go by: the figures add up as the story goes, and the right-hand card tells each week in words. Useful for a review, an appeal, or to show how the product works.
about.HLP1010: Search for a word to find the screens that talk about it, or start a guided tour: it opens the screens it needs and points at each button in turn. Press F1 on any screen for its own help.
about.HOME: The home page shows the day at a glance: people, leave, positions, what needs attention, the latest hires and the latest activity. Everything on it opens the screen behind it.
about.LEV1010: The yearly days and the carry-over are settings of the company; confirm them against the labour law and the contracts.
about.LEV2010: An approved leave shows on the roster and in attendance. The days are counted on working days of the person's calendar. Nobody approves their own leave.
about.LEV3010: The entitlement is the yearly days of the leave type plus what can be carried over from last year for people hired before the year.
about.ORG1010: The organisation tree. Pick a unit to see its people, positions and sub-units; add a unit below the one selected. A unit is never really deleted: it goes to the Recycle Bin with its history.
about.ORG1020: A job is what a person does (Welder, HR officer). A position is one seat of a job in one department. Mark the critical jobs: the Advisor and the plan can then warn when they are uncovered.
about.ORG1030: One position holds one person. A vacant position is shown in the Advisor as a tip; two people in one position is an error to correct.
about.OVT1010: Overtime is approved before it is worked, and never by the person it is for. Kinds: day, night, rest day, holiday.
about.OVT1020: Minutes by kind, the premium rates from the policy, and substitute days owed for rest-day work. Time worked beyond the plan without an approved request is listed as an exception. HR does not pay; it only states the figures.
about.REC1010: Plans are entered by people or proposed from the crew needs GMES sent (average heads per line and month plus a relief allowance). A plan someone entered is never overwritten by a proposal.
about.REC1020: A request goes draft, approved, open, filled. The person who raised it cannot approve it. A request above the headcount plan needs a note saying why.
about.REC1030: Move a candidate stage by stage. Hire is possible only after an offer: it creates the employee, the contract and the onboarding checklist in one step. Only a name is kept here; no personal data.
about.REC1040: Medical check, protective equipment and ESD training must be done before a new hire can be scheduled on a production line. Mark items done here or by passing the matching course.
about.REC1050: Agencies are kept so agency workers and their contracts can be traced to a supplier.
about.REC1060: Fixed-term contracts end on their last day: the button ends the expired ones and the employee becomes Terminated.
about.SEC9010: Each person has one user and one profile. A new user must change the first password at the first sign-in. The Advisor warns when a user holds two rights that should be separated.
about.SEC9020:
Tick the actions a profile may do, or start from a template, then save. The rights are checked by the server on every request, not only hidden on the screens.

Some pairs of rights should not sit with one person (for example managing users and changing employee records): the screen warns about them. The administrator profile always holds every right.
about.SEC9030: Every sign-in, refusal and change is written here and can never be edited or deleted. The line at the top says whether the chain is intact.
about.SHF1010: A night shift that ends after midnight counts as one work day: the day it starts. The times of a shift people already worked cannot change; create a new shift instead.
about.SHF1020: A calendar says which week days are rest days and which dates are holidays. The week starts on Saturday, as in Egypt.
about.SHF2010: A regular assignment never overlaps another regular one; a temporary one covers it for a period. An assignment that already started can only be ended, not changed.
about.SHF3010: The planned week, computed from the assignments, the calendars and the day changes. Click a day to change it (with a reason) or swap two people. The past is history: a day before today cannot be re-planned.
about.SHF3020: Choose a period and press Inquiry. Every planned day gets a verdict: as planned, absent, no record, on leave, worked a day off. Filter or group by the verdict column to find the problems quickly.
about.SKL1010: Define a skill once; give it a validity in months if certificates must be renewed.
about.SKL2010: Use the presets above the grid to see what expires soon or has expired. The expiry follows the validity of the skill unless you set a date.
about.SKL3010: One row per person, one column per skill. Click a cell to certify or re-certify. Expired qualifications are red; manufacturing refuses an unqualified person at a station that requires the skill.
about.STF2010: For each day and shift: heads GMES needs on every line, heads HR scheduled, and for each required skill how many hold it valid. Expired qualifications do not count. Red rows are short.
about.SYS9060: Server settings apply to everyone. Your own preferences (theme, look, density, language) stay in this browser.
about.SYS9070: A backup is made automatically at the interval set in Settings, and each one is restored in a safe place to prove it works. A restore never overwrites data: it writes a new, compensating change.
about.SYS9100: The journal, the audit, the last backup, the recovery installer and the signing library, each with a clear verdict.
about.TRN1010: Passing a course grants or renews the matching qualification. A course never lowers a level a person already holds.
about.TRN2010: Enter the employee codes of the attendees, then record pass or fail once the session has taken place. A pass grants the qualification and completes the matching onboarding item.

tip.employee: A person's employment data only: personal data (birth date, national id, pay) is never kept here. The position places them in the structure and gives their department and job.
tip.employee_skill: Leave the expiry empty: it follows the skill's validity. Level 3 means the person works alone; level 4 means they can train others.
tip.penalty_rule: Example: warning,deduct:0.25,deduct:0.5,deduct:1 - the 4th time and after deducts one day. A deduction is at most 5 days.
tip.position: One position holds one person. It belongs to a department or section and may report to another position: that is the reporting line.
tip.shift_assignment: A regular assignment never overlaps another regular one; a temporary one covers it for a period and needs an end date. Once it has started, only its end date can change.
tip.violation: Enter a misconduct by hand; late arrivals and absences are proposed from attendance. The line manager decides it within 30 days.
